findings.title: Whitearmor Ransomware Attack on Maersk - DeXpose
findings.summary_md: DeXpose reports that the Whitearmor ransomware group publicly claimed responsibility for a cyberattack against Maersk on November 7, 2026, threatening to leak data unless a $5 million ransom is paid. The post summarizes the victim as a Danish logistics company with about 100,000 employees across roughly 130 countries.

findings.title: maersk - claimed by Whitearmor
findings.summary_md: Ransomware.live recorded on 2026-11-07 that maersk was claimed by the Whitearmor ransomware group. The listing asserts approximately 100 GB of data taken from Maersk's OCF / LF Logistics platform and a $5,000,000 bitcoin demand with a 30-day deadline.

findings.title: WhiteArmor Maersk Claim Unverified - CyPro
findings.summary_md: CyPro reports that the WhiteArmor Maersk claim appeared on an extortion leak site on 7 November 2026, alleging theft of about 100 GB of logistics data. The claim remained unverified and unsupported by publicly available evidence as of 23:59 UK time that day.

findings.title: whitearmor claims 100GB Maersk logistics data breach - f4n6
findings.summary_md: f4n6 reports that on 2026-11-07 the extortion group Whitearmor posted a claim on ransomware.live asserting roughly 100 GB taken from Maersk's OCF / LF Logistics platform and demanding USD 5,000,000 in bitcoin within 30 days. The claimed data includes 16,093 driver records with plaintext passwords, 16,123 staff accounts including 33 SUPER_ADMIN accounts, and 27,842 mobile device logs.

findings.title: Maersk confirms data breach attributed to WhiteArmor
findings.summary_md: HIFY Radar reports that WhiteArmor listed Maersk on its leak site claiming theft of about 100 GB from a platform linked to the former LF Logistics business and demanding $5 million. Maersk later confirmed a data breach following the claim.
